question: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis is most effective when the first dose is given within 60 minutes before skin incision to ensure adequate tissue levels at the time of bacterial contamination.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. Prophylactic antibiotics must be given within 60 minutes before incision (within 30 minutes for vancomycin and fluoroquinolones) to achieve bactericidal tissue levels at the time of surgical contamination.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Current evidence supports administration of prophylactic antibiotics within 60 minutes before incision (30 minutes for vancomycin/fluoroquinolones) to achieve peak tissue concentrations during the contamination window.
